subject: general
question:
Directions: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

Rohit Rajan the DSP of Agra (A)/ is come (B)/ to dinner. (C)/ No Error(D)
solution:
The correct answer is **__B__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**.

__
 
• "**Come**" is (**simple) present tens**e. Use it when you are talking about a habit,** e.g**., "She always comes to my house on Friday nights."
 
• Here the sentence is in **present continous tense** and the structure of present continuous tense is **Sub+is/are/am+ verb+ing+ object.**
 
• So the error is in part B, where we need to use '**coming'** in place of '**come'**.
 
• Hence, **option 2** is the correct answer.

**The correct sentence is:** *Rohit Rajan the DSP of Agra is **coming **to dinner.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here, the sentence can be explained as:

 
• Is coming = verb (verbal phrase).
 
• is = auxiliary verb.
 
• coming = present participle.
 
• Rohit Rajan the DSP of Agra = subject.
 
• to dinner = adverbial (prepositional phrase) functioning as an adverbial phrase of place modifying the verb “is coming.”
 
• to = preposition heading the prepositional phrase “to dinner.”
 
• to = preposition showing a connection or link between “someone” and “dinner.”
 
• dinner = object of the preposition “to.”
